_doc: Board lesson templates. Mohit 2026-10-07: 'from the board pick the thing and end the lesson, these are our templates'. Sentence one names something measured on the board; sentence two is the lesson and never changes, because that is the part the player keeps. docs/board_lesson_templates_scope.md

hanging_ignored.board: Your {victim} on {victim_square} was attacked by the {attacker} on {attacker_square}, and nothing was defending it.
hanging_ignored.lesson: Look at what they attack before you start your own plan.

moved_the_guard.board: Your {mover} on {from_square} was defending your {victim} on {victim_square}. It left, and {capture} takes it.
moved_the_guard.lesson: Before you move a piece, check what it is holding.

landed_uncounted.lesson: Count attackers and defenders before you put a piece on a square.

opened_line.board: Moving off {from_square} opened the line from the {attacker} on {attacker_square} to your {victim} on {victim_square}.
opened_line.lesson: When a piece steps aside, look down the line it just left.

capture_available.lesson: Look at every capture before anything else.

king_square_theirs.board: The {enemy} comes to {landing_square}, next to your king. Your king cannot take it there, because the {guard} on {guard_square} guards that square. Then it takes your {victim} on {victim_square}.
king_square_theirs.lesson: A square next to your king is only safe if nothing of theirs guards it.

king_square_theirs_check.board: The {enemy} comes to {landing_square}, next to your king, with check. Your king cannot take it there, because the {guard} on {guard_square} guards that square. You have to answer the check, and then it takes your {victim} on {victim_square}.
king_square_theirs_check.lesson: A square next to your king is only safe if nothing of theirs guards it.

forked.board: Their {attacker} lands on {landing_square} and attacks your {first} on {first_square} and your {second} on {second_square} at the same time.
forked.lesson: One piece can attack two of yours at once. Before you move, look for the squares that would hit two of your pieces.

capture_window_closed.board: {best_san} takes the {target} on {target_square}, and right now more of your pieces hit that square than theirs defend it. After {reply} that is no longer true.
capture_window_closed.lesson: A capture that is there now is often gone next move, so count before you play something else.
